as_read: Conflicting evidence with no clear benefit: controlled lipid and cognition results are null, and the positives are within-group, secondary or one scale among several.

quote.text: Evidence from randomized trials does not support the use of lecithin in the treatment of patients with dementia.

proposed_decision_text: A Cochrane review of twelve randomized trials reports no clear clinical benefit of lecithin in Alzheimer's or Parkinsonian dementia, though one trial in subjective memory problems favored it (12917896). A double-blind trial of 20 g/day soya bean lecithin in 20 hyperlipidaemic men found no independent effect on serum lipoproteins (9683394), and an exploratory trial of five emulsifiers including soy lecithin found no cholesterol difference from placebo (40816342). The evidence conflicts, with no clear benefit: a 500 mg/day capsule trial reports total and LDL cholesterol falls of 40% to 56% from baseline, not a between-group effect (21490917); 20 g/day raised the HDL/LDL ratio from baseline with no difference in flow-mediated dilation (17006376); 1200 mg/day improved vigor and two cardiovascular measures while a fatigue scale was unchanged (29310653); a lecithin fluid missed its main target measure and improved a secondary responder measure (15662899); and soybean lecithin 10 g three times a day was reported effective in acute cerebral infarction in a study that doesn't state randomization (16200721). No trial of sunflower lecithin was found.
